name: Right Here
tagline: You thought you had to choose. You never did.
epigraph: Four plants flavour this gin, they say. The last you taste comes first here.
glassware: plain kitchen tumbler (about 250 ml), three or four ordinary ice cubes from the freezer tray
language_row: Wren's 4-gram runs against every pour: clean after seven cuts (*No Accident* "and here's the part", *Whoever Comes In* "deserves to be said", *As It Was* "the people around you", *Straight Up* "syrup as a nod", and others). No "we", no bare "yours" for the drink; "he/his" only for Nichol (lint warnings accepted by Wren). "Liquorice" (British) in every guest-facing line. *One of Us* failed lint ("I, not us") and was withdrawn. Never "genius", "promoted", "made good", escape or Billy Elliot. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/tom-nichol-tanqueray.md`: *Oxford Companion* NICHOL, TOM (pdf 1388, Robertiello), TANQUERAY GORDON & CO. (pdf 1985–1987, Frost), MASTER DISTILLER (pdf 1261), LICORICE (pdf 1673); Becky Paskin, *The Spirits Business*, 22 Feb 2013 (his words); Theodora Sutcliffe, *Difford's Guide*, Oct 2015; the Gin Guild's profile and 2015 Lifetime Achievement news; *Difford's* Cameronbridge producer page; Tanners (41.3% vol). Craft: *Liquid Intelligence* p. 125 (built drinks); *Cocktail Codex* pp. 2, 6 (Old-Fashioned template, garnish). Audits: `work/regular-guy-creator/historian-audit-v1.md`, `-v2.md`, `-v3.md`. Room notes: `work/regular-guy-creator/`.
names_note: **Right Here**, the room's pick (all three): the gift came up where he already was (he joined the gin team "there"), and it tells the guest they can keep their place. Also considered: *Close to Home* (Wren's r4 pick, conceded in r5: "close to home" usually means "that stings", and it echoes *Brought Home* in this family), *One of Us* (failed lint: one bartender says "I"), *Both* (withdrawn: can read as a reproach), *Kept Close* (reads as hiding), *Who Knew?*, *Last Comes First*, *Just a Hint*, *The Fourth One*, *Two Stills*.
open_items: **Contains nuts (Tomás, safe side):** Oxford pdf 1673 says the licorice plant is a legume, the peanut's family; our veto list has no legume class, and nothing clears liquorice. Shared packing is a second reason. Wren questioned it in r3 and accepted it in r5. Robin's call.
**Strength edge:** the US Tanqueray (47.3%) puts it at 32.8%, the top edge; the recipe note says 50 ml at 47% or stronger (31.9%). UK bottle 41.3% (*Difford's*, Tanners), not 43.1%.

**Hedges that must travel:** Tanqueray's four botanicals are "purportedly"/"said to" (Oxford). No. Ten is never his; the Malacca revival gets no year; winter savory is Charles Tanqueray's c. 1880 recipe; "his spirit went into the Tanqueray" is inference, left out.

**Our reading, not the record:** no page says anyone doubted him, so "unseen" is the room's reading; he "wore his heart on his sleeve", so never "he kept it quiet" (the hiding is the guest's only). The two praised later gins are in the dossier, not the reading.
**Image brief:** the distillery across the rooftops is a symbol, never captioned as his home (Cambus closed 1993).
**No garnish, owned in Checks:** peel would put citrus on a gin said to have none.
